messages:
Jai (support): FYI customer 'BrightCart' opened a ticket — their SSO flow when embedded in an iframe ends up in a perpetual reauth loop. Happening on Chrome 110+ and Safari iTP-enabled browsers. They say login appears successful but page immediately sends them back to /login.

Marina (infra): Can you paste the flow logs and the Set-Cookie headers from the auth callback? Sounds like state/nonce isn't being preserved.

Jai (support): Pasted below (redacted):

--- curl -i -X GET 'https://auth.redwood.ai/authorize?client_id=bc&response_type=code&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.brightcart.com%2Fauth%2Fcallback' -H 'Origin: https://app.brightcart.com'
HTTP/2 302
location: https://idp.example.com/login?state=xyz
set-cookie: _redwood_sess=eyJ..; Path=/; Domain=auth.redwood.ai; Max-Age=300; HttpOnly

--- idp redirects back to auth callback (iframe)
HTTP/2 200
set-cookie: _redwood_sess=eyJ..; Path=/; Domain=.redwood.ai; Max-Age=300; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
POST /auth/callback -> 302 -> /app (inside iframe)
then app immediately issues GET /session/verify -> 401 {"error":"invalid_nonce"}

Jai (support): Customer sees the callback succeed but our session verify call shows missing nonce/csrf cookie in the request from the iframe.

Omar (sre): Last time we saw similar it was SameSite/Lax blocking the cookie in cross-site subframe navigation. Chrome's default will block third-party cookies unless SameSite=None; Secure is set. The Set-Cookie above is SameSite=Lax which prevents the cookie being sent on the POST from inside an iframe. Also note the domain mismatch (auth.redwood.ai vs .redwood.ai) — could be multiple cookies being set and the browser choosing the wrong one.

Liam (eng): Also check nonce rotation TTL. Our auth service issues a short-lived nonce (60s) stored server-side + client cookie. If the iframe flow takes >60s (idp redirect + user MFA), nonce expires and callback fails with invalid_nonce even if cookie present. What does the customer's timing look like?

Jai (support): They say MFA prompt adds ~90s. So that matches.

Marina (infra): Repro steps I used locally:
1) curl -c jar -b jar -i -L 'https://app.local:8443/' -H 'Origin: https://app.brightcart.com'
2) follow redirect to /authorize and complete idp redirect (simulated)
3) at the callback I see cookie not sent on subsequent XHR from iframe.

Marina (infra): DevTools trace snippet (Chrome network):
Request: POST https://app.brightcart.com/session/verify
Request headers include: origin: https://app.brightcart.com, referer: https://app.brightcart.com/iframe-host
Cookie header: (missing)

Response: 401 {"error":"session_missing_csrf"}

Liam (eng): Two likely contributing issues: 1) SameSite default prevents cookie on cross-site POST from iframe. 2) Nonce TTL too short for slow MFA flows. Fix plan: set SameSite=None; Secure on auth cookie, unify domain to .redwood.ai for callback path, and increase nonce TTL to 5 minutes. But we should also recommend avoiding iframe-based auth flows — OIDC best practice is top-level redirect or using postMessage + top-level auth.

Omar (sre): Also watch for Safari ITP and 3rd-party cookie blocking — if the customer's app blocks third-party cookies entirely, SameSite=None won't help. For those cases we need a top-level reauth flow or a token exchange in the parent frame.

Jai (support): I provided repro steps to BrightCart and asked if they can switch to top-level redirect as a test. They asked for a patch on our side since they can't change the integration quickly.

Liam (eng): I pushed a quick patch to the auth service in staging:
- set-cookie: _redwood_sess=...; Domain=.redwood.ai; Path=/; Max-Age=259200; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None
- nonce TTL bumped to 300s
- added explicit cookie pruning to remove legacy auth.redwood.ai cookie

session-bot: deploy status: staging auth-service v1.12.3 -> SUCCESS :white_check_mark:

Marina (infra): Deployed patch to staging. Reproduced with an iframe test harness that simulates 2-step MFA and long delays — cookie is now present on POST and session verify succeeds.

Jai (support): Sent patched build to BrightCart support instructions:
- test on Chrome 115+ with third-party cookies allowed (temp)
- we recommend switching to top-level redirect for permanent fix
- if customer can't do redirect, we can keep SameSite=None cookie and longer nonce but warn about Safari 3rd-party blocks

BrightCart (customer) later: "Patch worked — login no longer loops. Thanks for quick turnaround." :thumbsup:

Liam (eng): Follow-ups:
- Create runbook entry: "iframe-embedded SSO reauth loop" covering detection (missing cookie on XHR + invalid_nonce), mitigation (SameSite=None, increase nonce TTL), and recommended long-term fix (top-level OIDC redirect or parent frame token exchange).
- Add automated check in our QA harness to simulate slow MFA and ensure nonce TTL > median MFA time.

Jai (support): I'll close the support ticket once runbook + PR numbers are linked. Thanks team. :party_parrot:
